title: How can we cut a trapezium into a rectangle?
description: An isosceles trapezium is cut at the midpoints of its slanting sides, and the two corner pieces turn half way round into the gaps above them. The pieces make a rectangle of the same area, as tall as the trapezium and as long as half the sum of the parallel sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: cut at the midpoints of the slanting sides and turn each corner piece about its midpoint. Watch for students who cut anywhere along the slanting side, because then the pieces do not fit.

source: Convert an isosceles trapezium to a rectangle by cutting it into pieces, from the Sulba Sutras
video_script.why: The child has seen a trapezium cut into a square and a triangle and now moves cut pieces to make a rectangle of the same area.
video_script.substitution: The book question gives no numbers, so the sides are called the top side, the bottom side and the height.
video_script.anchor: an isosceles trapezium with its top side, bottom side and height marked
video_script.payoff_line: It becomes a rectangle. Its height is the same, and its length is half the sum of the parallel sides.

final_answer.value: rectangle of height h and length 1/2 × (a + b)
final_answer.spoken: a rectangle as tall as the trapezium and as long as half the sum of the parallel sides

maths_rules: isosceles trapezium: slanting sides equal, top side a, bottom side b, height h
mark the midpoint of each slanting side
through each midpoint draw the line at right angles to the parallel sides
each line cuts off a small corner triangle below the midpoint; it is congruent to the gap triangle above the midpoint (equal angles at the midpoint, right angles, equal halves of the slanting side)
turn each corner triangle half way round about its midpoint into the gap above it
the result is a rectangle of height h and length 1/2 x (a + b), with the same area as the trapezium
video_script.design: One isosceles trapezium stays all video. The midpoint lines cut a small triangle off each bottom corner, and each triangle turns half way round about its midpoint into the gap above it, so the pieces make a rectangle.
